title: Interview evidence brief and skills decision trellis
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight, practical template + decision trellis for capture and faster role/no-role decisions. Intended for early People Ops + hiring manager syncs during small-to-mid hiring loops (IC-1 through senior IC). Focus: concise evidence capture, normalized rubric signals, and a small decision trellis to map risk vs. hire-conviction.

When to use:
- Immediately after first technical interview that includes a live exercise or take-home.
- Before the hiring manager scoring meeting (so data is ready for a 15–30 minute sync).
- When candidates are close but teams disagree on fit; trellis helps locate root mismatch.

Quick instructions (1-pager):
1) Interviewer fills the top section in < 6 minutes right after the interview.
2) People Ops owner (recruiter or interview coordinator) synthesizes any conflicting notes into the Trellis view.
3) Hiring manager completes the final yes/hold/no decision using the Trellis axes and adds a short rationale.

Template: Interview evidence capture (copy/paste into interview form)
- Candidate: [first last]
- Role: [title] / Hiring manager: [name]
- Date / interviewer: [date] / [interviewer name]
- Interview format: [livecoding | system-design | behavioral | take-home]

Core evidence (short bullets, factual):
- Prompt/context given to candidate: "..."
- Observable behaviors (3 bullets):
  - e.g., breaks problem into subproblems, asks clarifying Qs, references library X
  - e.g., stalls on concurrency tradeoffs; eventually proposes mutex + queue
  - e.g., communicates tradeoffs with cost/latency focus
- Outcome artifacts: [link to take-home gist or paste minimal diff] or [none]

Normalized rubric (1–4 scale) — capture numeric + 1-sentence reason (helps automated aggregation):
- Technical correctness (1-4): [score] — reason
- System design / architecture sense (1-4): [score] — reason
- Problem solving / decomposition (1-4): [score] — reason
- Communication & collaboration (1-4): [score] — reason
- Culture / alignment signals (1-4): [score] — reason (note: keep separate from performance metrics)

Bias-aware note: separate observable behavior evidence from inference. Underline direct quotes or artifacts. If you infer motivation or culture fit, mark as "inference".

Decision trellis (novel, practical):
Purpose: map two independent axes to guide outcome and next steps quickly. This is intentionally small (2 axes) to reduce discussion overhead.
Axes definition (each scored -2 to +2):
- Risk (how likely is the hire to cause rework / require close coaching across first 90 days): -2 (very low) .. +2 (very high)
- Conviction (how confident we are candidate will deliver core 60–90 day milestones): -2 (very low) .. +2 (very high)

How to use the Trellis:
- Plot candidate on (Risk, Conviction). The quadrant determines the recommended action.
  - Quadrant A (Low risk, High conviction): Hire (fast-track compensation/offer template A).
  - Quadrant B (High risk, High conviction): Consider hire with mitigations (probation goals + mentor pairing + smaller initial scope); propose a 12-week outcomes plan.
  - Quadrant C (Low risk, Low conviction): Hold for additional evidence (another scoped exercise or cross-functional interview).
  - Quadrant D (High risk, Low conviction): No-hire (or decline, unless extremely strategic reason).

Examples (short):
- Candidate X: Risk 0, Conviction +2 => Hire (notes: strong architecture, missing product nuance but low risk).
- Candidate Y: Risk +2, Conviction +2 => Hire-with-guardrails (notes: senior but inexperienced with infra constraints; propose pair-programming weeks 1–3).
- Candidate Z: Risk -1, Conviction -1 => Additional evidence (schedule a 60-minute design pairing).

Mitigation playbook (if we hire in high-risk cells):
- Explicit 30/60/90 milestones written into offer packet.
- Mandatory mentor pairing (SRE or peer) for first 6 weeks.
- Weekly check-ins with hiring manager + People Ops for first 4 weeks.
- Reduced initial scope by gating access to production-critical services for first 30 days.

Ramp / onboarding checklist (first 14 days minimal):
- Pre-start: hardware request sent? SSO/KMS access checklist initiated?
- Day 0: Welcome doc + team slack intros + buddy assigned
- Day 1: Dev environment build verified + access to internal model catalog sandbox
- Week 1: Small first-ticket assigned (non-prod), mentor pairing schedule set, calendar blocked for weekly 1:1
- Week 2: Code walkthrough with product + infra owners, deploy/runbook shadow session scheduled

Signals to watch (30/60/90):
- 30d: completes first ticket end-to-end, PR quality consistent with team norms, shows consistent local testability
- 60d: delivers a scoped feature or improvement with instrumentation and tests; participates in on-call rotation shadow
- 90d: independently owns a mid-sized component and drives a postmortem or design doc

Hiring conversation guide (for the 15-minute manager sync)
- Share the evidence bullet list (2 minutes).
- State Trellis placement (30 seconds) + rationale.
- Ask manager to pick recommended action (hire / hire-with-guardrails / more-evidence / decline).
- If manager asks for change, capture explicit missing evidence and owner for getting it.

Recordkeeping + acceptance protocol
- Recruiter updates candidate status in ATS and attaches this document.
- For hires, ensure mitigation playbook is added to onboarding packet if applicable.
- For declines, short rationale saved (1–2 sentences) to help calibration mailto list.

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- We need a small Airtable export template to visualize trellis across a panel (action: Evan Morales).
- Confirm the 1–4 scale wording against engineering rubric (action: Sofia).
- Decide whether Trellis axes should be numeric -2..+2 or 1..5 for compatibility with ATS (action: People Ops).

Appendix: quick scoring cheatsheet (one-liners)
- Technical correctness 4 = correct, edgecases covered, unit test checklist noted; 1 = broken or unsafe approach.
- System design 4 = clear end-to-end, non-trivial tradeoffs, capacity/latency thought; 1 = shallow component sketch.
- Problem solving 4 = decomposes, iterates, returns to goals; 1 = stuck despite hints.
- Communication 4 = clear narrative + admits uncertainty + invites collaboration; 1 = opaque or dismissive.

Notes to self: keep this doc compact. This is intentionally lean to encourage completion. If teams like this pattern, we can convert to a micro-form integrated in the hiring tracker.

Document history:
- Author: Priya Nair (People Ops)
- Drafted: 2025-11-04
- Coaching edits: 2025-12-12 (Sofia Alvarez)
- Panel trial run: 2026-01-28 (updated trellis wording)
- Last revised: 2026-02-10

Copy/paste ready checklist for interviewers (one line):
"After interview: add 3 factual bullets, score five rubric items 1–4 with 1-sentence rationale, paste any artifact link, place candidate on Trellis (-2..+2), note recommended action."
